rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to present the Book as clear guidance for everything that leads to right guidance.
rows.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بالإبانة لكل ما يوجب الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion established the sender's complete knowledge of the unseen and visible and the reach of His power in word and deed.
rows.anchor: من تمام علم منزله غيبا وشهادة وشمول قدرته قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah demonstrated the Quran's divine origin and God's power to punish nations, unite some people, divide others, and grant victory to His servants.
rows.anchor: عظيم قدرته على مثل ما عذب به الأمم وعلى التأليف بين من أراد وإيقاع الخلاف بين من شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long story of Joseph is especially apt to make these purposes clear, which explains the surah's name.
rows.anchor: هذه القصة - كما ترى - أنسب الأشياء لهذا المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, al-Raḥmān's mercy leaves no obscurity in the universal path of guidance.
rows.anchor: الذي لم يدع لبسا لعموم رحمته في طريق الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, al-Raḥīm singles out His party by keeping them away from the place of ruin.
rows.anchor: الذي خص حزبه بالإبعاد عن موطئ الردى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's ordeal by his closest relatives, strangers, exile, and family separation ends in the finest outcome through patience and entrusting matters to God, consoling the Prophet.
rows.anchor: تسلية لهذا النبي الأمين وتأسية بمن مضى من إخوانه المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's brothers intended the same kinds of harm that the Prophet's pagan relatives considered: restraining, killing, or expelling him.
rows.anchor: ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك أو يخرجوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God later gave Joseph control over his brothers, the story foreshadows the Prophet's victory at the conquest of Mecca, when he overcame and pardoned his opponents.
rows.anchor: ثم نصر الله يوسف عليه السلام على إخواته الذين فعلوا به ذلك وملكه قيادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story signals that an envied person can be raised when he acts as he ought, and warns that envy can overwhelm even righteous people unless they repent promptly.
rows.anchor: الحسد داء عظيم شديد التمكن في النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's story alone is not repeated elsewhere so that the lives of eminent figures are not used to suggest flaws, invite attacks, or trivialize envy.
rows.anchor: تركت إعادتها دون غيرها من القصص صونا للأكابر عن ذكر ما ربما أوجب اعتقاد نقص

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says the disconnected letters are not counted as verse endings because two-letter forms do not resemble the verse endings; Ṭā Hā is counted because it does.
rows.anchor: قال الروماني : لم تعد الفواصل لأنها لا تشاكل رؤوس الآيات لأنها على حرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī rejects the claim that Quranic verse endings were composed as sajʿ, since that would associate the Quran with the soothsayers' craft.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول من ذهب سهوا إلى أن السجع مقصود في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted counting of verse endings is based on received instruction, like the transmission of readings.
rows.anchor: مرجعها التوفيق مثل نقل القراءات سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eloquent opening demonstrates a text whose meanings exceed exhaustive human understanding while still presenting an intelligible meaning from first reflection.
rows.anchor: على أن يأتي بما يفهم به أوائل النظر أدنى معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening responds to the opponents' accusation of fabrication and indicates that the Quran was sent with God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ودل على أنه أنزل بعلمه , ابتدئت هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah signals the Quran's elevated rank and distance from ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: بالإشارة إلى ما له من علو المحل وبعد الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points both to the preceding Quran and this surah, while the disconnected letters pose a puzzle that becomes clear on reflection.
rows.anchor: مشكلة التي ألقاها بالأحرف المقطعة وبان أنها مع إشكالها عند التأمل واضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is comprehensive of all intended meanings, clear in itself, miraculous, and unmistakable to Arabs; deep reflection discloses everything it contains.
rows.anchor: البين في نفسه أنه جامع معجز لا يشتبه على العرب بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description mubīn means both that the Quran is clear in itself and that it makes its contents clear.
rows.anchor: والموضح لجميع ما حوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description links to the Quran's denial of fabrication and its confirmation of earlier revelation, and to its role as admonition and reminder.
rows.anchor: ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayān separates a meaning from other meanings, while burhān additionally displays evidence that the meaning is true.
rows.anchor: ويزيد عليه البرهان بأنه إظهار صحة المعنى بما يشهد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic phrase says God sent down the Book, using descent in the context of the opponents' denial; the pronoun can refer to this surah or the whole Quran.
rows.anchor: بنون العظمة أي الكتاب المفسر بهذه السورة أو بالقرآن كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran is a generic name that can refer to the whole revelation or to a part of it.
rows.anchor: سمي بعضه بذلك لأن القرآن اسم جنس يقع على الكل والبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic is the most eloquent, capacious, upright, and balanced language; speech addressed to one group can apply generally to others.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن اللسان العربي أفصح الألسنة وأوسعها وأقوامها وأعدلها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says laʿalla, although normally expressing hope, carries the sense of purpose here.
rows.anchor: أبو حيان و ( لعل ) ترج فيه معنى التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ can mean the best telling or the best narrated story; the account unfolds in sequence with especially clear explanation.
rows.anchor: أي الاقتصاص أو المقصوص بأن نتبع بعض الحديث كما نعلمه بعضا فنبينه أحسن البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This narrative confirms the Prophet's mission and steadies him through its order, completeness, precise exposition, and subtle meanings in foundational and practical matters.
rows.anchor: تثبيتا لفؤادك وتصديقا لنبوتك وتأييدا على أحسن ترتيب وأحكم نظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is exceptionally long in the Torah, where only specialists can master it; attentive readers can recognize the Quran's superior narration.
rows.anchor: هي في التوراة في نيف وعشرين ورقة لا يضبطها إلا حذاق أخبارهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that a Torah-reading Jewish scholar found the Prophet reciting Joseph's story as revealed in the Torah; the scholar and his companions converted after verifying the Prophet's description and seal.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( أن حبرا من اليهود دخل على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative highlights Joseph's good treatment of his brothers, patience, forbearance, overlooking their reproach, and generous forgiveness.
rows.anchor: حسن مجاورة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام لإخوته وصبره على أذاهم وحلمه عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story encompasses prophets, righteous people, angels, devils, humans, jinn, animals, rulers, subjects, merchants, scholars, ignorant people, and women.
rows.anchor: والأنبياء والصالحين والملائكة والشياطين والإنس والجن والأنعام والطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its lessons include monotheism, prophethood, inimitability, dream interpretation, governance, social relations, livelihood, and benefits for religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: والتوحيد والنبوة والإعجاز والتعبير والسياسة والمعاشرة وتدبير المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike other narratives, Joseph's story contains no extraneous story material and concludes in safety, reunion, forgiveness, and divine pardon for all.
rows.anchor: وكان عقابها إلى خير وسلامة واجتماع شمل وعفو من الله وتجاوز عن الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase bima awḥaynā means that this account comes by God's revelation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب إيحائنا { إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming this revelation as this Quran answers the charge of fabrication: its successive stories and judgments make its divine origin increasingly unmistakable.
rows.anchor: فنحن نتابع فيه القصص بعد قصة والحكم حكمة في أثر حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had not known this story or others before revelation, despite the opponents' familiarity with his distance from learning and scholars.
rows.anchor: الغافلين } أي عن هذه القصة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī explains the root gh-f-l through the semantic field of concealment and covering, as in an envelope that hides what is inside.
rows.anchor: ومادة , غفل , بكل ترتيب تدور على الستر والحجب

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr introduces this surah as one of the accounts of earlier messengers that steadies the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : هذه السورة من جملة ما قص عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike earlier accounts of messengers' missions and the destruction of their rejecting peoples, Joseph's story centers on relief after hardship and patience's good outcome.
rows.anchor: أما هذه القصة فحاصلها فرج بعد شدة وتعريف بحسن عاقبة الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob is tested by losing two sons, his sight, and the scattering of his children; Joseph by the pit, sale, the wife of al-ʿAzīz, separation from family, and prison.
rows.anchor: امتحن يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام بفقد ابنيه وبصره وشتات بنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family reaches poverty and need, then God reunites them, restores Jacob's sight, reconciles their hearts, undoes Satan's division, and clears Joseph.
rows.anchor: ثم تداركهم الله بالفهم وجمع شملهم ورد بصر أبيهم وائتلاف قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eventual relief follows Joseph's beautiful patience, certainty, and submission to divine decrees throughout prolonged trials.
rows.anchor: جميل صبره وجلالة اليقين في حسن تلقي الأقدار بالتفويض والتسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story also includes the wife of al-ʿAzīz's repentance and truthful testimony that God had granted Joseph purity, followed by the ruler's release of him.
rows.anchor: إنابة امرأة العزيز ورجوعها إلى الحق وشهادتها ليوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story stands alone because its core is the eventual relief and lesson of patient endurance, unlike the surrounding accounts of other prophets' peoples.
rows.anchor: فقد انفردت هذه القصة بنفسها ولم تناسب ما ذكر من قصص نوح وهود وصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's story resembles the early believers' suffering, migration, estrangement, and poverty before God gathered them together.
rows.anchor: أشبه شيء بحال المؤمنين في مكابدتهم في أول الأمر وهجرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' faith and patience brought them unity, inheritance of the land, support, and victory, explaining why this distinct story follows the preceding narratives.
rows.anchor: ذلك بجليل إيمانهم وعظيم صبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after Hūd also follows the instruction to do good, be patient, and wait for God's judgment amid disagreement and opposition.
rows.anchor: ثم ناسبت سورة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام أيضا أن تذكرإثر قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' remorse and confession that Joseph was favored by God, along with Joseph's later pardon, exemplify a good deed removing an evil deed.
rows.anchor: ندم إخوة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام واعترافهم بخطاء فعلهم وفضل يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's pardon of his brothers and the wife of al-ʿAzīz's admission that truth had emerged also exemplify good deeds erasing wrongs.
rows.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفرالله لكم } ) 77 [ يوسف : 92 ] وندم امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: نبينا
rows.claim: The Prophet said that, had he remained in prison as long as Joseph, he would have answered the caller; Biqāʿī cites this as testimony to Joseph's patience.
rows.anchor: قول نبينا وقد ذكر يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام فشهد له بجلالة الحال وعظيم الصبر فقال ( ) ولو لبثت في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph and Jacob exemplify the patience commanded in Hūd; Joseph is counted among the resolute messengers whom the Prophet was told to emulate.
rows.anchor: فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their patience and worldly vindication parallel the Prophet's hardship with Quraysh, migration from his homeland, later victory, and return honored with his companions.
rows.anchor: ثم تعقب ذلك بظفره بعدوه وإعزاز دينه وإظهار كلمته ورجوعه إلى بلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the surah's ending clarifies his argument about patience, presenting its final message as further evidence.
rows.anchor: ويوضح ما ذكرنا ختم السورة بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discord among Joseph's brothers, all sons of one prophet and righteous servant, is a striking lesson connected to the statement that people remain divided.
rows.anchor: حال إخوة فضلاء لأب واحد من أنبياء الله تعالى وصالحي عباده جرى بينهم من التشتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to opponents is as if to say that the believers will not endure them for as long as Jacob and Joseph endured their trials.
rows.anchor: فلن نصبر عليكم مدة صبر يعقوب ويوسف عليهما الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase idh begins the account of the time when Joseph spoke to his father, explaining the preceding promise of the best narrative.
rows.anchor: أي نقص عليك خبر إذ , أي خبر يوسف إذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative yā abatī conveys Joseph's good manners toward his father, whose high rank and momentous subject merit close attention.
rows.anchor: ومن بين أدبه بقوله - مشيرا بأداة البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers stop at the tāʾ marbūṭa in yā abatī with hāʾ; its kasra signals the omitted possessive yāʾ, while fatḥa substitutes for the alif standing for it.
rows.anchor: تاءه للتأنيث لأنه يوقف عليها عند بعض القراء بالهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was young and the dream momentous, so the expression inni raʾaytu is emphatic; ruʾyā denotes seeing during sleep.
rows.anchor: ولما كان صغيرا , وكان المنام عظيما خطيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven kawākib are conspicuous, large, bright stars.
rows.anchor: أي نجما كبيرا ظاهرا جدا مضيئا براقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating raʾaytu and using a rational plural for the celestial bodies emphasize the dream's strangeness and their acting like rational beings in prostration.
rows.anchor: زاد في الإشارة إلى ذلك بإعادة الفعل , وألحقه ضمير العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of repetition of Joseph's story rebuts those who explain repetition elsewhere as a way to reinforce eloquence; repetition elsewhere also rebuts the claim that this one was omitted to preserve eloquence.
rows.anchor: تمكينا لفصاحتها بترادف السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's tender yā bunayya shows his compassion, while he knows the brothers will envy Joseph if they hear what the dream signifies.
rows.anchor: عالما بأن إخوته سيحسدونه على ما تدل عليه هذه الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that backbiting is not forbidden when used for sincere counsel and may even be recommended.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أنه لا نهي عن الغيبة للنصيحة

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines a dream as an imagined perception during sleep, when the sleeping mind pictures a meaning as if it were seen.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : والرؤيا : تصورالمعنى في المنام على توهم الإبصار

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says that when outward senses rest, inward faculties perceive unseen matters; they may perceive them directly or through symbolic likenesses requiring interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام الرازي في اللوامع : هي ركود الحواس الظاهرة عن الإدراك

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī distinguishes truthful dreams, which have interpretation, from false dreams, which do not; he applies this account to non-prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : والرؤيا الصادقة لها تأويل , والرؤيا الكاذبة لا تأويل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan makes enmity clear by inflaming fears of lost advantage, especially among prominent people; because dreams are difficult to interpret, one should tell them only to a compassionate, trustworthy adviser.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن تقص إلا على شفيق ناصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob understands from the dream that Joseph will attain prophethood and rule, and tells him that God will choose him as He chose him for this vision.
rows.anchor: ولما علم يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام من هذه الرؤيا ما سيصير إليه ولده من النبوة والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's choosing Joseph means selecting him and gathering for him the highest matters, nurturing him toward kingship and prophethood.
rows.anchor: يجتبيك } أي يختارك ويجمع لك معالي الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl al-aḥādīth includes interpretation of dreams, books and traditions of prophets, and hidden meanings in spiritual and bodily creation; rule and prophethood require such knowledge.
rows.anchor: من الرؤيا وغيرها من كتب الله وسنن الأنبياء وغوامض ما تدل عليه المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl is the point to which a meaning leads and the understanding of a report's wisdom; its most common use is for dreams.
rows.anchor: وذلك فقه الحديث الذي هو حكمة لأنه إظهار ما يؤول إليه أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes His favor on Joseph through prophethood, justice, and adherence to the straight way, and on Jacob's family by joining worldly blessing to the next life.
rows.anchor: ويتم نعمته } بالنبوة { عليك } بالعدل ولزوم المنهج السوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars in Joseph's dream signify his brothers and selected descendants; āl is used for people of distinction, whereas ahl is used for those without standing.
rows.anchor: ولا يستعمل الآل إلأ فيمن له خطر وشرف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib regards the reported phrase āl al-ṣalīb, if transmitted accurately, as anomalous; ahl is used for those without distinction.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : وأما آل الصليب إن صح نقله فشاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's blessing was friendship with God and other honors; Isaac's was prophethood and a line of prophets and kings.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم } أي بالخلة وغيرها من الكرامة { و } ولده { إسحاق } بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing a blessing means decreeing its lasting in a pure state, without anything that diminishes it.
rows.anchor: وإتمام النعمة : الحكم بدوامها على خلوصها من شائب فيها بنقصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing names al-ʿAlīm and al-Ḥakīm suit the need for complete knowledge of causes and wisdom in ordering them.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر عليه إلا بالعلم المحيط بجميع الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to God's unseen knowledge in Hūd supports the names al-ʿAlīm and al-Ḥakīm; wisdom is placing things in their most exact positions.
rows.anchor: الآية بليغ الحكمة , وهي وضع الأشياء في أتقن مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers first consider killing Joseph or throwing him into an unknown land where he will perish, if they are too scrupulous to kill him directly.
rows.anchor: أو اطرحوه أرضا } أوصلوا الفعل بدون حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their aim is for their father's attention, purpose, and intention to become exclusively theirs.
rows.anchor: يخل لكم } أي خاصا بكم { وجه أبيكم } أي قصده لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to become righteous after Joseph is gone by restoring harmony, earning their father's love through care, and repenting of the envy that breeds further sins.
rows.anchor: بالتوبة من ذنب واحد يكون سببا لزوال الموجب لداء الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed brother advises against murder, which is the greatest sin after associating partners with God, and proposes leaving Joseph in the well for a passing caravan to find.
rows.anchor: لا تقتلوا يوسف } لا بأيديكم ولا بالإلقاء في المهالك , فإن القتل أكبر الكبائر بعد الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker remains unnamed to show that sincere advice should be voiced by anyone and that no one should belittle himself for offering it.
rows.anchor: فقال مبهما إشعارا بأنه يجب قول النصح من أي قائل كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well's hidden depths are enough to conceal Joseph; the plan need only make him disappear until some travelers pick him up.
rows.anchor: في غيابت الجب } أي غوره الغائب عن الأعين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr says this episode occurred before the brothers became prophets.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو : إن هذا كان قبل أن يكونوا أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers persist and feign surprise that Jacob will not entrust Joseph to them, claiming they are sincere advisers.
rows.anchor: إعمالا للحيلة في الوصول إليه , مستفهمين على وجه التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere counsel is a sign and cause of trust, as in the description of Hūd's message.
rows.anchor: والنصح دليل الأمانة وسببها , ولهذا قرنا في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amn is inward calm that evil will not occur, encouraged by a long delay without the expected harm; the ignorant may be deceived by that delay, and its opposite is fear.
rows.anchor: والأمن : سكون النفس إلى انتفاء الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣḥ is sincere action kept free of intentional corruption, while its opposite is deceit.
rows.anchor: والنصح : إخلاص العمل من فساد يتعمد , وضده الغش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers assimilate the nūn of taʾmannā after its vowelless form in keeping with the written form; some use pure assimilation and others add ishām or rawm.
rows.anchor: وأجمع القراء علىحذف حركة الرفع في تأمن وإدغام نونه بعد إسكانه تبعا للرسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assimilation subtly signals that Jacob's heart is not at rest about entrusting Joseph to them, despite their apparent grounds for trust; pronouncing the ḍamma would lose the allusion.
rows.anchor: دلالة على نفي سكون قلبه عليه عليهما الصلاة والسلام بأمنه عليه منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask to take Joseph to their pasture so he can eat, drink, and enjoy the fertile countryside, play at lawful pleasures, and be guarded well.
rows.anchor: يرتع } أي نأكل ونشرب في الريف ونتسع في الخصب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says ghadan is an adverb for the next day or for future time generally; its original form ghadu lost its final letter.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وانتصب { غدا } على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says separation from Joseph will cause him real grief; the emphatic wording signals that he cannot bear even a moment apart.
rows.anchor: إني ليحزنني } أي حزنا ظاهرا محققا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob fears a wolf may eat Joseph while the brothers are distracted by grazing and their own concerns, since wolves were common in the area.
rows.anchor: الذئب } أي هذا النوع كأنه كان كثيرا بأرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines grief as heartache over separation from a beloved, especially when the separation is toward something hated, and eating as cutting food by chewing after swallowing.
rows.anchor: والحزن : ألم القلب مما كان من فراق المحبوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers answer the wolf concern with an emphatic oath: as a strong band, they would be complete losers if they failed to protect their brother.
rows.anchor: لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They avoid answering Jacob's concern about separation because a direct answer would expose their envy and could block their plan.
rows.anchor: وأعرضوا عن جواب الأول لأنه لا يكون إلا بما يوغر صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They all resolved, each with full determination, to put Joseph in the well; the narrative omits their carrying it out because the circumstances make it obvious.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا } أي كلهم , وأجمع كل واحد منهم بأن عزم عزما صادقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires Joseph with a firm promise that he will later tell his brothers what they did while they fail to recognize him because time will transform their appearance and circumstances.
rows.anchor: لتنبئنهم } أي لتخبرنهم إخبارا عظيما على وجه يقل وجود مثله في الجلالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Jurayj, as quoted by al-Rummānī, explain that the brothers will not recognize Joseph when he later tells them.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والحسن وابن جريج على ما نقله الرماني

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Joseph was twelve years old when his brothers cast him into the well.
rows.anchor: كان يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام حين ألقوه في الجب ابن اثنتي عشرة سنة - قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later scene confirms the promise: Joseph taps the measuring cup and says it tells him that they had a paternal brother named Joseph whom they threw into a well.
rows.anchor: فقال : إنه ليخبروني هذا الجام أنه كان لكم أخ من أبيكم يقال له يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaʿr means perception of a thing as subtle as a hair, and the term for the bodily senses derives from that comparison.
rows.anchor: والشعور : إدراك الشيء مثل الشعرة في الدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveling party arrives; its water-drawer, a delegate sent to inspect the well and fetch water, lowers his bucket, and Joseph clings to it and is pulled out.
rows.anchor: فأرسلوا واردهم } أي رسولهم الذي يرسلونه لأجل الإشراف على الماء إلى الجب ليسقي لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalla means lowering the bucket, while dallā means bringing it back up full; Joseph catches hold of the rope and is drawn out.
rows.anchor: وأما ( دلى ) فأخرجها ملأى - فاستمسك بها يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام فأخرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water-drawer calls for good news, as though summoning it to come, then announces that he has found a boy.
rows.anchor: أي هذا أوانك فاحضري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water-drawer and companions conceal Joseph as supposed merchandise, while God knows what they are doing.
rows.anchor: أي الوارد وأصحابه { بضاعة } أي حال كونه متاعا بزعمهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān infers that Joseph was young because a bucket rope would not usually lift a youth of seventeen or eighteen; ghulām strictly spans infancy to puberty, though it can also mean an adult.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان ونعم ما قال : وتعلقه بالحبل يدل على صغره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root lexicon says shara and shari can mean buying or selling: one gives up ownership while another acquires it, and the exchange can operate in either direction.
rows.anchor: فمن مطلقة : شريت الشيء , بمعنى ملكته بالبيع , وشريته , بمعنى : أزلت ملكي عنه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī glosses shirwa as an equivalent, connecting it to the matching value sought in exchange.
rows.anchor: وشروى الشيء : مثله واوه مبدلة من ياء كأنه مأخوذ من بدل المبيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī derives the many forms of sh-r-y and related permutations from insistence or persistence that spreads outward, sometimes implying strength and sometimes weakness.
rows.anchor: تدور على اللجاجة , وهي التمادي في الانتشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives describe lightning spreading, anger persisting until it blazes, and a horse pressing on at speed.
rows.anchor: وشرى البرق : استطار , وزيد : غضب ولج حتى استطار غضبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī treats shiryā, meaning a way or disposition, as a basic branch from which the other senses grow.
rows.anchor: والشرية - كغنية : الطريقة والطبيعة , وكأن هذا أصل المعنى الذي عنه تفرعت أغصانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The date palm's growth from its kernel, apparently without human intervention, is another example of persistence in spreading.
rows.anchor: والنخل ينبت من النواة , كأنه لنباته بغير سبب آدمي لجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī relates the sharyān tree used for bows to its force and the spreading flight of arrows shot from it.
rows.anchor: والشريان من شجر القسي , كأنه لقوته ونشره السهام إذا رميت عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He associates shiyār, Saturday, with the first day of creation, from which creation spread.
rows.anchor: وشيار - بالكسر : يوم السبت , لأنه أول يوم ابتدئت فيه الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same root covers spreading or dispersal, as in clouds breaking apart and other derived terms.
rows.anchor: وتشرى السحاب : تفرق , والشرى : شجر الحنظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related rīsh vocabulary is explained through spreading over the body, including plumage, clothing, abundant growth, and provision.
rows.anchor: والريش بالكسر - من الطائر معروف كالراش - لأنه منتشر في جميع بدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The derivative shāra ilayhi means gesturing toward something, which Biqāʿī links to spreading the sign of what is indicated.
rows.anchor: وشور إليه : أومأ كأشار - لنشر ما أشار به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī explains consultation and advice through extended speech or gesture aimed at finding and communicating a sound judgment.
rows.anchor: وأشرت عليه بكذا : أمرته للانتشار في الكلام قبل الإشارة للوقوع على الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats a bribe and its payment as inducing someone to act through persistence in a matter or through weakness.
rows.anchor: والرشوة - مثلثة : الجعل , ورشاه : اعطاه إياها , فنشره للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamzated form rashāʾ denotes intercourse and is explained as the strongest kind of persistence or extension.
rows.anchor: ومن مهموزه : رشأ : جامع , ولا ألج من المتهيىء للجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the related forms of b-kh-s and neighboring roots revolve around scarcity, often linked with taking by the handful; bakhasa means to reduce someone's due.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( بخس ) بكل ترتيب من بخس وخبس وسبخ وسخب تدور على القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples include an eye being put out as a specific loss, a tax, salty land with little growth, and cotton being reduced by cutting.
rows.anchor: بخسته حقه : نقصته فجعتله أقل مما كان , والبخس : فقء العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The w-r-sh family includes senses of eating eagerly and persistent appetite, which Biqāʿī connects with persistence and insistence.
rows.anchor: وورش الطعام : تناوله وأكل شديدا حريصا , وطمع وأسف لمداق الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links the loss of a bird's feathers and severe sleep to deficiency, depletion, and reducing a person's heaviness.
rows.anchor: والتسبيخ : النوم الشديد - لنقصه صاحبه وتخفيفه ما عنده من الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked forms kh-b-s and s-kh-b mean taking by the fist or an ornament lacking gems, continuing the association with deficiency and scarcity.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الخبس , وهو الأخذ بالكف - وهو لازم للقلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Bakhṣ is clarified as a small, deficient price, with countable dirhams rather than dinars; Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the price was twenty dirhams.
rows.anchor: روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها كانت عشرين درهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in they were among those who were indifferent refers to the caravan: they seized the chance to sell Joseph cheaply before others identified or reclaimed him.
rows.anchor: وهذا يعين أن الضمير للسيارة لأن حال إخوته في أمره فوق الزهد بمراحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhd means turning one's desire away from an object toward something the person considers better.
rows.anchor: والزهد : انصراف الرغبة عن الشيء إلى ماهو خير منه عند الزاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian purchaser tells his wife to honor Joseph's residence, a stronger instruction than merely honoring him, so he will want to stay with them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أعظم من الأمر بإكرامه نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchaser hopes Joseph will benefit them or, if he proves worthy, that they may adopt him as a son.
rows.anchor: ينفعنا } أي وهو على اسم المشتري { أو نتخذه } أي برغبة عظيمة إن رأيناه أهلا { ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enabling Joseph in Egypt is compared to how earlier He made the caravan and buyer honor him; Egypt is described as like the whole earth because of its abundance and his just rule.
rows.anchor: مكنا ليوسف في الأرض } أي أرض مصر التي هي كالأرض كلها لكثرة منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates Joseph's kingship through the implication of establishment in the land and his prophethood through the mention of divine teaching.
rows.anchor: وأثبت التمكين في الأرض ليدل على لازمه من الملك والتمكين من العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the interpretation of reports means leading their outward appearances back to their inner meanings.
rows.anchor: من تأويل الأحاديث } أي بترجيعها من ظواهرها إلى بواطنها
